children: Soybeans are picking up after Friday's selloff on the USDA's bigger harvest estimate. While ending stocks are comfortable, "what happens if China would buy more beans from the U.S.? Or what would happen if South America has a little weather issue to cause them to have a smaller crop this year?" Cory Bratland of AgMarket.net says in a note. With funds holding a record long position and harvest starting, prices could consolidate, "but keep a close eye on the weather in South America and also, keep a close eye on the meeting between President Trump and President Xi on Sept. 24," he adds. CBOT soybeans are up 1%. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
